findings.what: The topping stage holds 2.35 V a cell, which the scale shows inside the yellow band labelled 'boost', but screen 8 then presents boost as something different and compares it only with charging 'at the float setting the whole way', so no sentence says how a normal charge differs from a boost and Dan is left asking which one screen 2 was.

findings.where: SHOW screens 2, 6, 8 and 10 (task text plus the live line under the control)
findings.what: Screen 2's text is 92 words and is followed by a 22-word live line that repeats its own last two sentences; screens 6, 8 and 10 come to about 107 to 113 words with their live lines, and the 33-word lead paragraph sits above every screen, which is the 'too much text after the diagrams' Dan asked to stop.

The task never says which temperature rule applies, and the lesson also teaches that one maker leaves the setting alone from 10 to 30 °C, so '2.25 V' is a defensible answer at 15 °C; state the 3 mV a cell per degree from 25 °C rule in the task (and say the cells, not the room, are at 15 °C, which also fixes the awkward 'This cell floats at 2.25 V a cell').

findings.where: Whole lesson against the brief's lesson 4 row
findings.what: Two items the brief promised as syllabus items for this lesson are missing: charge efficiency (recharge about 1.2 times the ampere-hours taken out, so about 83 per cent come back) and the planned last screen, the simple charging circuit from a DC supply; neither appears in i1 to i3 either.

The lesson carries nine [^n] marks (eight in explain, one in practice), far more than 'a few a lesson', including [^12] on the bold summary sentence, which is not a value he would look up; keep the three or four figures he would check (2.25 V float, 3 to 5 per cent, 2.50 V equalise, 3 mV per °C).

findings.where: Screen 3 hint and why, screen 10 text, explain (five times)
findings.what: 'One common rule' and 'one maker' repeat as hedges and read like source talk; give the figure as typical ('A cell counts as full when...', 'A typical correction is 3 mV a cell...') and keep the single 'follow the battery's own maker' line.

findings.where: Screen 4 'Times the cells' and the explain's matching paragraph
findings.what: 'Each takes the same current. So you choose the setting for one cell' does not follow; the reason is that the band belongs to one cell's chemistry and series cells add their volts.
'A corroded positive grid' after one weekend overstates the harm; 'extra grid corrosion, and water lost as gas' is true without being absolute.
'boil off water' is wrong in kind, because the water is split into gas by the current, not boiled; say 'split water off as gas'.

It describes 'the trace' on the bank screens where no trace is drawn and 'one drawn cut open' on the trace screens where no cut cell is drawn, and on screen 8 it says 'held at 2.35 V' while the trace boosts at 2.38 V.
'Still there.' is cryptic; 'That's it: 12 × 2.25 = 27.00 V.' says what he got right.
The fifth cell box and its two links vanish in one frame while the '…' fades in, so the string jumps instead of settling.

Practice says a boost makes gas, but the pictures show no bubbles at the 2.38 V boost (bubbles start only at 2.40 V); one line that gas climbs steeply near 2.40 V while a boost near full still gasses a little would reconcile them.

The 2.23 to 2.27 V band joins a maker's 20 °C figure with a 25 °C figure, while screen 10 shifts the whole band from a 25 °C reference; it reads fine as a sketch, but the bottom edge is not a 25 °C value.
The hints for '0 A' and 'Nothing' restate the right answer outright ('calls it full when the current falls to 3 to 5 per cent', 'That current corrodes the grid'), so a second try needs no thought.
'adds it back below' is unclear, so say 'adds 3 mV a cell for each degree below'; and 'the picture is simplified' in the explain talks about the lesson rather than the battery.
